title: Vector search + Rerank deep dive — Horizon Retail
summary: Deep technical session focused on embeddings dimensionality, batching/throughput tradeoffs for vector search + reranking, latency SLOs, KV cache behavior for generative rerankers, quantization options, and VPC/on-prem constraints. Agreed to run a pico-benchmark with 1k synthetic queries versus 10k real queries, test int8 vs 4-bit quantization, and validate end-to-end 95th percentile latency under 200ms for search+rerank. Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet and security docs.
topics: KV cache impact for rerank / generative models
VPC / on-prem deployment constraints (KMS, egress, air gap)
cost per qps / per-embedding unit vs Dedicated capacity
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Diego, Sara, Liam, Nisha (Horizon Retail)
Notes/links: Shared benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/s/hr-vector-benchmark, security packet: redwood.com/sec/hr (shared)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — we'll kick off with a short agenda: vector dims, batching, rerank latency, then discussion on on-prem/VPC constraints.
[00:18] Diego: thanks, Jordan. high level we want vector search + a light generative reranker for product recommendations, targets are sub-200ms p95 end-to-end at 200 qps, and cost needs to be reasonable given we run peak holiday spikes.
[00:32] Priya: sounds good, can you run me through your current infra? are you using FAISS on VMs, or a managed vector DB?
[00:44] Diego: currently FAISS on GCP instances (n1-like), flat index for accuracy, we store 10M product vectors at 1,024 dims. Searching is fine but we see rerank adding a lot of latency.
[00:58] Sara: the reranker is an LLM-based scorer — we send top-k 50 candidates and the model returns scores and a short justification. our current p95 with rerank is ~700ms which is too high.
[01:12] Marcus: ok, good context. couple of early pres: for embeddings dims, 1,024 is common but 768 can be close in quality for a lot of retail use-cases and is cheaper per vector (memory & compute). 1,536 gives more signal but increases index size and CPU/GPU costs.
[01:28] Liam: memory is the main limit — our FAISS nodes already hit 80% mem on peak. moving dims down could be attractive.
[01:40] Priya: when you say rerank, is it a generation-heavy workflow (i.e., full token logits and KV cache) or a lightweight scoring model?
[01:52] Sara: it's closer to generation — we ask the model to return a natural language justification and a score. so we have to run decoding for each candidate or do a rerank-by-batch where we score the top-50 in a single prompt.
[02:10] Jordan: right, so tradeoffs are: run one batch prompt that includes 50 items -> bigger prompt tokens but single model call, or call model per-item which gives more parallelism but higher per-call overhead.
[02:24] Diego: what's Redwood's recommendation for batch sizes for the rerank?
[02:30] Priya: empirically we've seen best latency vs cost at batching ~8-16 candidates per model call for decoder-style rerankers on H100/A100 backends. for higher throughput you can go to 32-64 but p95 starts to rise because of token-length variance.
[02:48] Marcus: also kv cache only helps within a single request when you decode step-by-step; it doesn't help across independent rerank calls. so if you do one big prompt with 50 items, you still pay for the long context but the decoder can reuse prefixes if the prompt is structured. if you do 50 separate calls you can't share kv across calls unless you pin a session (complex).
[03:10] Liam: pin a session — is that something Redwood supports on Dedicated?
[03:16] Priya: yes, on Dedicated/private you can maintain pinned inference sessions which keep a warmed KV cache per model instance, useful for many short decodes where you reuse the same system prompt. but it's stateful and shouldn't be used for multi-tenant setups without careful isolation.
[03:28] Nisha: our security team would demand KMS integration and no ephemeral egress — we need to understand the VPC private deployment options.
[03:36] Jordan: we'll cover that in the later part; short answer: Redwood Private supports customer VPC peering, KMS, and an on-prem appliance for air-gapped installs.
[03:46] Diego: back to numbers — if we go from 1024 to 768 dims, what's the roughly expected reduction in memory and latency?
[03:56] Marcus: rough ballpark: memory per vector reduces proportional to dimension, so 25% reduction moving 1024->768. CPU search time roughly scales down as index fits better in cache — maybe 10-30% faster depending on index type (IVF+PQ vs flat). For GPU-based vector search, reduction is similar but depends on GPU memory and batching.
[04:18] Sara: how does vector dimension affect quality? we're worried about moving too low on dims.
[04:24] Priya: we usually recommend A/B testing 768 vs 1024 on your recall/CTR metrics. for product retrieval, many customers see small quality delta; the bigger lever is index type (PQ levels, nprobe) and reranker quality.
[04:38] Diego: ok. and on rerank latency, what are expected per-call latencies for a 1B param reranker on A100?
[04:46] Marcus: for a 1B decoder model on A100 with batching of 8 and short outputs (<= 40 tokens) you can expect ~40-80ms per batch at typical settings; p95 depends a lot on tokenization variance — p95 could be ~120-200ms. For larger models e.g., 7B, numbers scale up: single-batch p50 may be 150-250ms, p95 considerably higher.
[05:12] Sara: our SLO is 200ms p95 end-to-end at 200 qps — is that realistic with rerank?
[05:20] Priya: it is if you optimize: use small reranker (<=1B) or distilled ranker, batch candidates (8-16), use prefix caching for the system prompt, and run embedding nearest-neighbor on a fast vector index with SSD-backed shards or GPU-based ANN. Also warm caches prior to peak.
[05:40] Diego: can you quantify cost — e.g., dollars per 1k qps or per-100k queries?
[05:46] Jordan: rough numbers: hosted per-embedding call is $0.0004 to $0.001 (depending on model & dims) and rerank calls vary: small reranker might add $0.001-$0.005 per request at hosted rates. on Dedicated, unit economics depend on reserved GPU pools. For example, an A100 cluster sized to handle sustained 200 qps rerank could look like tens of thousands per month in committed cost but gives much lower per-query compute cost.
[06:12] Liam: can Redwood provide a sample cost model?
[06:16] Jordan: yes — we'll share a calc in the benchmark sheet for 768 vs 1024 dims and different reranker sizes.
[06:22] Nisha: we need to evaluate quantization — can we run the reranker quantized to int8 or 4-bit safely?
[06:28] Marcus: yes, quantization options depend on model architecture. For many transformer decoders you can do int8 with little quality loss; 4-bit (GPTQ-style) is feasible but requires a calibration step. Redwood supports quantized variants in Dedicated/private and we can recommend bit-width vs accuracy tradeoffs. We saw 2-3x throughput improvement moving from fp16 to int8 for some models.
[06:52] Sara: how about latency variance introduced by quantization? any negatives?
[06:56] Priya: generally quantization reduces latency, but it can increase tail latency variability if kernels are not well-optimized on the hardware. Redwood's runtime picks optimized kernels; for H100/A100 quantization kernels are stable but we'll validate in your benchmark.
[07:12] Diego: about KV cache — our reranker sometimes needs to run 50 short decodes, can we benefit from KV caching across those?
[07:20] Marcus: KV helps if decodes are incremental and share a common prefix within a single request. If you do 50 independent decodes with different inputs you'll get less benefit. Two patterns: 1) single prompt that lists the 50 candidates, decode once and parse outputs; 2) maintain pinned sessions to keep the model warm and reuse prompt prefixes — that'll reduce per-call startup but uses memory.
[07:44] Liam: pinned sessions sound stateful; our infra team worries about isolation between customers when we run multi-tenant Dedicated.
[07:52] Priya: pinned sessions are per-customer on Private/Dedicated. On hosted multi-tenant we don't expose pinned KV sessions to customers for security and fairness reasons. For Dedicated you can reserve instances and have per-customer sessions.
[08:06] Nisha: security: if we go on-prem we need HSM/KMS integration and audit logs, retention policies, and the ability to disable egress. Does Redwood provide these?
[08:14] Jordan: yes — Redwood Private supports integration with customer KMS (KMIP/Cloud KMS), full audit logs, and an air-gapped option for on-prem. We'll share the security packet.
[08:24] Diego: can we talk about a concrete benchmark plan? what do you need from us?
[08:30] Priya: ideal inputs: sample traffic profile (qps, top-k search widths), a 10k query set representing real queries, and an evaluation metric (ctr, recall@k). Redwood will run three experiments: (A) 1024 dims + 1B reranker (batch=8), (B) 768 dims + 1B reranker (batch=16), (C) 768 dims + quantized 1B reranker (int8/4-bit) and measure latency p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k queries.
[08:58] Sara: we'll provide 10k queries and a small labeled set for quality metrics.
[09:02] Marcus: for the reranking prompt composition, please include the exact schema you plan to use (how you format candidates in the prompt) — small differences change token counts and perf.
[09:12] Diego: we'll share the prompt templates.
[09:14] Nisha: what about the vector DB — is the plan to keep FAISS or use Redwood's vector service?
[09:20] Priya: we can index on your FAISS cluster or use Redwood's managed vector service; managed offers GPU-ANN which is lower latency but you trade off vendor control. For on-prem, we can deploy a connector that keeps index local.
[09:34] Diego: any gotchas with FAISS + Dedicated GPU reranker in terms of network hops?
[09:40] Marcus: network hop cost matters — ideally co-locate FAISS index and reranker in the same VPC region or on the same cluster to avoid cross-AZ latency. If FAISS is CPU-only and reranker is GPU, make sure throughput from search to rerank is local. We saw 10-30ms variance across AZs.
[09:58] Sara: can we estimate end-to-end p95 for plan B (768 dims + quantized reranker) at 200 qps?
[10:06] Priya: rough estimate: ANN search p95 ~20-50ms (GPU-ANN) or 50-120ms (CPU-FAISS), rerank p95 with batching and quantization ~80-140ms. Combined, you're looking at 100-200ms depending on search infra. The quantized reranker gives us headroom. We'll validate with the benchmark.
[10:28] Diego: if we need <150ms p95, what's the safest approach?
[10:32] Marcus: smallest safe route: 1) use 768 dims with GPU-ANN + localized index, 2) distilled reranker ~500M-1B params quantized to int8, batch 8-16, 3) pin sessions on Dedicated to reduce startup. That combo puts you comfortably under 150ms in many cases.
[10:52] Nisha: any tradeoffs for quality with distilled / quantized reranker?
[10:56] Priya: slight drop — maybe a few percentage points in rerank accuracy. That's why we need your labeled eval to judge. Often business metrics (CTR, conversion) don't degrade if the retrieval+rerank loop is well tuned.
[11:10] Diego: ok that makes sense. next steps?
[11:14] Jordan: agreed plan: Redwood to run the three benchmark variants, share spreadsheet with cost modeling, and propose a Dedicated cluster spec if results look good. Customer to provide 10k query set, prompt templates, and labeled eval.
[11:26] Sara: timeline?
[11:28] Jordan: we can start the benchmarks in 1 week once we have artifacts; deliver initial results in 7-10 business days.
[11:36] Liam: will you include on-prem deployment guidance in the report?
[11:40] Marcus: yes — we'll include deployment patterns (co-located FAISS + GPU rerank nodes, VPC peering, pinned sessions) and a recommended Dedicated sizing for sustained 200 qps.
[11:52] Diego: any competitor angle we should watch? we currently evaluate Pinecone and Vespa for vector search and did a quick eval of a managed reranker from CompetitorX.
[11:58] Jordan: noted. Redwood will compare expected cost/latency vs Pinecone + hosted rerank in the spreadsheet.
[12:06] Nisha: security docs again please — SOC2 toolset and audit examples.
[12:10] Jordan: will share security packet and SOC2 summary.
[12:14] Priya: quick note on monitoring: Redwood Console will give you token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, and we can surface rerank-specific traces so you can see top-k -> rerank timing.
[12:26] Diego: that will help. any final clarifications?
[12:30] Sara: small question — when you say batch 16 for rerank, do you mean 16 candidates per model call or 16 concurrent requests?
[12:36] Marcus: 16 candidates per model call. concurrency is separate — you can have many concurrent batched calls. we tune batch size for latency vs token length.
[12:44] Jordan: ok we'll recap.
[12:46] [meeting recap]
Jordan: action items and next steps: Redwood runs three benchmarks (1024/768/quantized), share cost model and Dedicated sizing, share security docs. Horizon will send 10k queries, labeled eval, and prompt templates. Redwood to schedule follow-up 30m review.
[13:10] Diego: thanks everyone, looking forward to the results.
[13:14] Jordan: thanks — we'll send the benchmark plan and invite for the follow-up.
[13:20] [end recording]
